nodes.label: package_consumer_smoke
nodes.rationale: The supported Windows MSVC release lanes keep package proof in the normal CTest graph while local game corpus checks remain opt-in.

nodes.label: libbsa_package_consumer
nodes.rationale: The post-build runtime-copy step keeps a shared-install consumer runnable without relying on source-tree paths.

nodes.label: libbsa Fixture Policy
nodes.rationale: Separates reproducible committed test evidence from copyrighted local game data without mutating the TES5Edit reference submodule.

nodes.label: Committed Generated Fixtures
nodes.rationale: Committed fixtures are tiny, legal, and generated specifically for tests so compatibility checks remain reproducible.

nodes.label: Local Game-derived Fixtures
nodes.rationale: Copyrighted game archives remain outside git and their tests are opt-in and skipped when no local fixture path is configured.

nodes.label: Benchmark Generated Data Policy
nodes.rationale: Benchmark evidence uses legal synthetic data so default acceptance does not depend on copyrighted local archives.

nodes.label: Fixture Provenance Requirements
nodes.rationale: Every committed fixture records its recipe, legal provenance, and the behavior it proves.

nodes.label: TES5Edit Read-only Boundary
nodes.rationale: TES5Edit is only a behavior reference and cannot be a mutable fixture workspace or source of committed fixture files.

nodes.label: Benchmark Harness
nodes.rationale: Maintainer tooling generates legal synthetic data, exercises serial and opt-in parallel workflows, and verifies correctness through public APIs.

nodes.label: Report-only Performance Policy
nodes.rationale: Host-dependent timing does not gate default CTest; correctness and report generation are the automated contract.
